root_cause.text: The `do_secure_storage_access` handler erroneously treated the absence of the `PG_arch_1` flag as confirmation that a page was already exported, preventing necessary secure storage fixups for donated memory and causing an infinite exception loop.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that for donated memory the `PG_arch_1` bit is absent, yet prior logic assumed absence meant "already exported," leading to "secure storage access exception loops which can never be resolved," while the patch introduces `uv_convert_from_secure` and proper error handling via `handle_fault_error_nolock`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `do_secure_storage_access` handler in `arch/s390/mm/fault.c` erroneously treated the absence of the `PG_arch_1` bit on donated memory as confirmation that the page was already accessible, bypassing required fixups and creating an infinite secure storage access exception loop.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces the call to `arch_make_folio_accessible()` (which returned immediately when the `PG_arch_1` bit was absent) with `uv_convert_from_secure()` and changes the error path from `BUG()` to `handle_fault_error_nolock()`, directly addressing the CVE description which states the previous logic caused "secure storage access exception loops which can never be resolved" for pages lacking the `PG_arch_1` bit.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `do_secure_storage_access` exception handler in the s390 memory management subsystem incorrectly interpreted the absence of the `PG_arch_1` bit as confirmation that donated memory was already exported, causing it to skip necessary secure storage fixups via `arch_make_folio_accessible()` and resulting in unresolvable exception loops.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description states that `arch_make_folio_accessible()` returns instantly when the `PG_arch_1` bit is absent, signifying "already exported," but for donated memory this bit is absent because the kernel isn't allowed to export it, leading to "secure storage access exception loops which can never be resolved."
